variants.asks: Einstein's field equation has one number in front of the source. What does this model put there instead?

steps.because: the rules, read as a line: every rule of the theory is a term, the reading having run each rule's program on a symbolic match and counted what it does to the population - what it makes, what it takes, what it carries, what a body puts in - so the line is what the rules come to as a crowd rather than a description of them. Everything a theorem of this theory stands on is a term of this line or a reading of one, so every premise below is read off it, and every derivation passes through it

the rule fires only where active, so whatever it does it does on that share of its matches and the term carries it

steps.via: what Einstein's coupling is multiplied by
steps.because: what Einstein's coupling has to be multiplied by to give this model's: 1 - A over 2\Phi. The held metric gives one, at every distance - the metric is sourced by the same potential the pull is, once through the falling body's speed and once through the square of its beat

derivation.via: the time part answers the potential
derivation.because:
EINSTEIN'S FIELD EQUATION, in the static field where it is a statement about one function: G_{\mu
u} = 8\pi G T_{\mu
u} comes to 1 - A = 2\Phi with 
abla^{2}\Phi = 4\pi Gho. The held clock beats at the falling body's beat, and that body's speed squared is twice the potential the pull integrates to - so 1 - A is 2\Phi, the whole of it and not its first order. The same ho sources it, through the same flux law, at Einstein's coupling

derivation.via: a clock held where a body falls
derivation.because: a clock held at r is passed by a body falling in from far at \beta^{2} = 2\Phi, and nothing tells the two apart but that speed: the falling one is what every body does there, the held one is moving against it. So the held clock beats at the falling body's beat, and the time part of the metric is that beat squared - 1 - \beta^{2} = 1 - 2\Phi. In the mass the pull fixes this is 1 - r_{s}/r, with r_{s} twice G m over D - 2: Schwarzschild's, the two not put in but the square of a beat

derivation.via: a body moves or it emits
working: MOVEMENT: every ray a cell a tick, so a body's step is c-bar whatever it does
a source moves or it emits: what it spends going, it does not spend shining
derivation.because: MOVEMENT steps every ray a cell every tick and never holds one back, and a body is rays turning - so a body's step is always the whole of c-bar, and what it spends going somewhere it does not spend standing where it is. What it sends it sends standing: a source moves or it emits, and on a tick it moves it does not shine the way it went. So its going and its standing share one step, at right angles - the going along its heading, the standing across it, where its rays turn - and the standing is its beat: \beta^{2} + \paren{d\tau/dt}^{2} = 1. Fore and aft it comes to the same: what it sends ahead is thinned by 1 - \beta and what it leaves behind by 1 + \beta, and the beat is the mean of the two, \sqrt{\paren{1 - \beta}\paren{1 + \beta}}

derivation.via: the mass is what the vacuum leaves over
derivation.because: the rays' line is linear in what a source puts in, so it solves for it: the share of l's ways a source lights is how the lit share at l moved, less what the vacuum's own rules did to it - put in by creation, taken by the meetings. Where the rays do only what the vacuum does, it is nought; anything else is a source

derivation.via: a body falling in from far
derivation.because: a body let go at rest far off gains speed as the pull does work on it: \frac{d}{dt}\frac{\beta^{2}}{2} = g·\beta, and the pull is the potential's slope - so at R its speed squared is twice the potential there. Every body falls so, whatever it is made of: the pull is the record's slope, and the record does not ask what crosses it

the pull integrated in from far off, where it is nought: one power of the distance weaker than the pull. It is the record the body left, in rays' worth and halved - so the potential is not a second field beside the record, it IS the record

derivation.via: the pull far from a body
working: n_{f,l} - n_{f}\paren{\rho_{\infty}} \to \frac{x.\bar{m}·D·\sigma·F·\rho_{\infty}·x.\bar{R}^{2 - D}}{2·\paren{D - 2}}, past the free path
derivation.because: what a body feels is the record's slope in rays' worth, g = \frac{1}{2}\nabla S_{l}, and S_{l} = 2n_{f,l}. Far from a body - past its free path, where the reach has died - the record it leaves is what the walk carries, one power of the distance weaker than the shell, so its slope falls as the shell does: the inverse square at three dimensions, at a strength that is the lattice's own and nothing chosen. G is the dimension over twice the free path

derivation.via: the record every body leaves at a local
working: the settled vacuum underneath: n_{f} at \rho_{\infty}, \frac{DEG_{0}·\rho_{\infty}^{2}}{4·\paren{1 - \rho_{\infty}}}
x = x_{@t}: every body at its own time, bound once in the sum; x.\bar{R} = l.distance\paren{x.l}, from the local now to the body then
the walk: CREATION lights all DEG of a point's ways, so a heading is drawn afresh; \lambda = \frac{1}{\sigma·F·\rho_{\infty}}, outward at \bar{c}·\paren{D - 2}\lambda / \paren{D·x.\bar{R}}
derivation.because: a meeting turns 2 of l's rays into a fold and a creation reads it back out, so l's rays, DEG of them a way, and 2 times its record move together: the meetings cancel out of their sum, and what is left is what the bodies put in and creation's share against the record l holds over its own ways - nought where the ways have settled, at \rho_{\infty}. So what a body puts in is never lost to the vacuum, only spread: what crosses the shell at a distance in a tick is what the body put out then, and the rays alone are the near field, what still arrives as rays, spread over the same shell - the record is the one less the other, so it is what the meetings took on the way, never less than nought. And what they took walks rather than streams - a creation reads it back out on every way at once - so it crosses each shell at c-bar (D - 2) lambda / (D R), lambda the free path, and beyond the free path stands 1/R^{D-2} deep: in three dimensions it falls as one over the distance, and its slope, the pull, as one over its square, over 2, on the settled record. Each body is read as it was when its rays left it, at its own distance then
